417: func runtimeEventDraft(req runtimepkg.Request, event runtimepkg.Event) runcontrol.EventDraft {
418: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
419: 	lowerType := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Type))
420: 	lowerKind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Kind))
421: 	switch lowerType {
422: 	case "warning", "warn", "error":
423: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
424: 	case "artifact", "file":
425: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventArtifact
426: 	case "finding":
427: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventFinding
428: 	case "message", "text", "output", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text", "reasoning", "content", "delta":
429: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
430: 	default:
431: 		// Kind-based fallback: reasoning and message kinds should be visible as message, not coalesced progress.
432: 		switch lowerKind {
433: 		case "message", "reasoning", "assistant", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text":
434: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
435: 		case "tool", "tool_use", "tool_call", "tool_call_update":
436: 			// Tools stay as progress but with distinct payload so coalescing can distinguish.
437: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventProgress
438: 		}
439: 	}
440: 	payload := map[string]string{
441: 		"runtime_event_id": boundedSafe(event.ID),
442: 		"runtime_run_id":   boundedSafe(event.RunID),
443: 		"session_id":       boundedSafe(event.SessionID),
444: 		"type":             boundedSafe(event.Type),
445: 		"kind":             boundedSafe(event.Kind),
446: 	}
447: 	if lowerKind == "tool" || lowerKind == "tool_use" || lowerKind == "tool_call" || lowerKind == "tool_call_update" {
448: 		captureToolObservation(payload, event.Payload)
449: 	}
450: 	// Preserve safe observable payload fields into durable storage for observability.
451: 	// Deny sensitive keys and truncate values to runcontrol-safe limits.
452: 	// Flatten one level of nesting so tool/action names buried in maps are surfaced as top-level payload keys
453: 	// that the run timeline JS expects (payload.tool, payload.action, payload.title, etc.).
454: 	for key, value := range event.Payload {
455: 		if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
456: 			continue
457: 		}
458: 		normalized := strings.TrimSpace(key)
459: 		if normalized == "" || len(normalized) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(normalized, "\x00\r\n") {
460: 			continue
461: 		}
462: 		if normalized == "type" || normalized == "kind" {
463: 			continue
464: 		}
465: 		if nested, ok := value.(map[string]any); ok {
466: 			for subKey, subVal := range nested {
467: 				if isSensitivePayloadKey(subKey) {
468: 					continue
469: 				}
470: 				subNorm := strings.TrimSpace(subKey)
471: 				if subNorm == "" || len(subNorm) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(subNorm, "\x00\r\n") {
472: 					continue
473: 				}
474: 				if _, exists := payload[subNorm]; exists {
475: 					continue
476: 				}
477: 				// Promote common observable sub-keys; namespace the rest to avoid collisions.
478: 				promote := map[string]bool{"tool": true, "title": true, "detail": true, "text": true, "delta": true, "content": true, "message": true, "action": true, "state": true, "status": true, "native_type": true, "line": true}
479: 				targetKey := subNorm
480: 				if !promote[subNorm] {
481: 					targetKey = normalized + "_" + subNorm
482: 					if len(targetKey) > 128 {
483: 						continue
484: 					}
485: 				}
486: 				if _, exists := payload[targetKey]; exists {
487: 					continue
488: 				}
489: 				str := payloadValueString(subVal)
490: 				if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
491: 					continue
492: 				}
493: 				if len(payload) >= 30 {
494: 					break
495: 				}
496: 				payload[targetKey] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
497: 			}
498: 			// Also keep a compact stringified top-level for debugging if not promoted.
499: 			if len(payload) < 30 {
500: 				if _, exists := payload[normalized]; !exists {
501: 					str := payloadValueString(value)
502: 					if strings.TrimSpace(str) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(str, "[map omitted") {
503: 						payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
504: 					}
505: 				}
506: 			}
507: 			continue
508: 		}
509: 		str := payloadValueString(value)
510: 		if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
511: 			continue
512: 		}
513: 		if len(payload) >= 30 {
514: 			break
515: 		}
516: 		if _, exists := payload[normalized]; exists {
517: 			continue
518: 		}
519: 		payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
520: 	}
521: 	// Ensure the most useful display keys are always present even if nested.
522: 	for _, want := range []string{"tool", "action", "title", "detail", "text", "delta"} {
523: 		if _, ok := payload[want]; ok {
524: 			continue
525: 		}
526: 		if v := findNestedString(event.Payload, want); v != "" {
527: 			payload[want] = boundedPayloadValue(v)
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	omission := (*runcontrol.Omission)(nil)
531: 	if event.RawPresent || event.RawOmitted {
532: 		reason := firstSafeValue(event.RawOmissionReason, "runtime payload omitted by safe persistence policy")
533: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe(reason), Count: 1}
534: 	} else if len(event.Payload) > len(payload)-5 {
535: 		// Payload had more fields than we persisted (truncated/omitted keys) – record for diagnostics but don't hide persisted fields.
536: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe("runtime payload truncated to safe observable fields"), Count: 1}
537: 	}
538: 	return runcontrol.EventDraft{
539: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeRuntime,
540: 		Stage: boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]), Task: boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"])),
541: 		Kind: payload["kind"], Tool: payload["tool"], Action: payload["action"],
542: 		Reason: payload["reason"], Detail: firstSafeValue(payload["detail"], payload["title"]),
543: 		Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
544: 	}
545: }

547: func isSensitivePayloadKey(key string) bool {
548: 	lower := strings.ToLower(key)
549: 	for _, marker := range []string{"secret", "token", "password", "authorization", "cookie", "api_key", "apikey", "credential", "auth"} {
550: 		if strings.Contains(lower, marker) {
551: 			return true
552: 		}
553: 	}
554: 	return false
555: }
556: 
557: func findNestedString(payload map[string]any, want string) string {
558: 	for _, v := range payload {
559: 		if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
560: 			if s, ok := m[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
561: 				return s
562: 			}
563: 			// One more level deep (common for opencode part.state structures)
564: 			for _, inner := range m {
565: 				if innerMap, ok := inner.(map[string]any); ok {
566: 					if s, ok := innerMap[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
567: 						return s
568: 					}
569: 				}
570: 			}
571: 		}
572: 	}
573: 	return ""
574: }
575: 
576: func payloadValueString(value any) string {
577: 	switch v := value.(type) {
578: 	case string:
579: 		return v
580: 	case []byte:
581: 		if len(v) == 0 {
582: 			return ""
583: 		}
584: 		return string(v)
585: 	case bool:
586: 		if v {
587: 			return "true"
588: 		}
589: 		return "false"
590: 	case int:
591: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
592: 	case int8:
593: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
594: 	case int16:
595: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
596: 	case int32:
597: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
598: 	case int64:
599: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
600: 	case uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64:
601: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
602: 	case float32, float64:
603: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
604: 	case map[string]any, map[string]string, []any, []string:
605: 		// Encode structured values compactly.
606: 		encoded, err := jsonMarshalTruncated(v)
607: 		if err != nil {
608: 			return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
609: 		}
610: 		return encoded
611: 	default:
612: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
613: 	}
614: }
615: 
616: func jsonMarshalTruncated(v any) (string, error) {
617: 	encoded, err := json.Marshal(v)
618: 	if err != nil {
619: 		return "", err
620: 	}
621: 	return string(encoded), nil
622: }

624: func captureToolObservation(out map[string]string, payload map[string]any) {
625: 	for target, aliases := range map[string][]string{
626: 		"tool_call_id": {"tool_call_id", "toolCallId", "call_id", "callID"},
627: 		"tool_name":    {"tool_name", "toolName", "tool", "name"},
628: 		"tool_status":  {"tool_status", "status", "phase"},
629: 	} {
630: 		if value := findNestedPayloadValue(payload, aliases, 0); value != nil {
631: 			if text, ok := value.(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(text) != "" {
632: 				out[target] = boundedPayloadValue(text)
633: 			}
634: 		}
635: 	}
636: 	for target, aliases := range map[string][]string{
637: 		"tool_arguments": {"tool_arguments", "arguments", "args", "input", "parameters"},
638: 		"tool_result":    {"tool_result", "result", "output", "content"},
639: 		"tool_error":     {"tool_error", "error"},
640: 	} {
641: 		value := findNestedPayloadValue(payload, aliases, 0)
642: 		if value == nil {
643: 			continue
644: 		}
645: 		encoded, err := json.Marshal(redactObservableValue(value))
646: 		if err == nil && string(encoded) != "null" {
647: 			out[target] = boundedPayloadValue(string(encoded))
648: 		}
649: 	}
650: 	if out["tool"] == "" {
651: 		out["tool"] = out["tool_name"]
652: 	}
653: }
654: 
655: func findNestedPayloadValue(value any, aliases []string, depth int) any {
656: 	if depth > 5 {
657: 		return nil

reasoning_details.text:
Very interesting. `sanitizeEventDraft` is the final storage gate. Note:

1. **`sensitiveEventField` denylist at storage level includes "payload", "prompt", "path", "command", "stdout", "stderr"** — but app-level allowlist in the runtime draft pipeline produces keys like... wait, storage uses an ALLOWLIST (`allowedEventPayloadFields`). Any payload key not in the allowed list is DROPPED (counted as omitted). So the app-level pipeline (run_control.go:454-520) can produce keys like `parent_child` namespaced keys (e.g., `part_text`), `provider`, `model`, etc. Only allowlisted keys survive: runtime_event_id, runtime_run_id, agentwrap_run_id, session_id, external_harness_run_id, type, kind, state, status, outcome, reason, category, code, count, known, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, turns, artifact_kind, artifact_id, lifecycle, liveness, message, index, scope, tool, action, detail, tool_call_id, tool_name, tool_status, tool_arguments, tool_result, tool_error, provider, model, harness, phase_state, summary.

Hmm wait — but sensitiveEventField ALSO applies to allowlisted keys: does any allowlisted key contain fragments? "tool_arguments" contains none of secret/token/credential/password/prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command. OK.

But here's a subtle one: app-level `RecordOperationEvent` builds payload with keys: state, type, count, phase_state, summary, tool_call_id, tool_status, tool_arguments, tool_result, tool_error, provider, model, harness — all allowlisted except... all are in list? state ✓, type ✓, count ✓, phase_state ✓, summary ✓, tool_call_id ✓, tool_status ✓, tool_arguments ✓, tool_result ✓, tool_error ✓, provider ✓, model ✓, harness ✓. Good.

For runtime drafts: identity keys runtime_event_id/runtime_run_id/session_id/type/kind ✓; captureToolObservation keys tool_call_id/tool_name/tool_status/tool_arguments/tool_result/tool_error ✓; generic loop keys arbitrary → mostly dropped at storage; promoted ones: tool/title/detail/text/delta/content/message/action/state/status/native_type/line — allowlist has tool ✓, action ✓, detail ✓, message ✓, state ✓, status ✓; title/text/delta/content/native_type/line ✗ dropped (omitted counter). So much of the app-level sanitization work is moot but harmless. Not a defect per se (omission metadata records it).

2. **`unsafeEventValue` rejects ABSOLUTE PATHS**: `filepath.IsAbs(value)` → true → field omitted. Also Windows drive paths. And values containing \x00\r\n. But note: app-level boundedPayloadValue strips control chars; storage safeEventValue also strips. Values with absolute paths get omitted with omission metadata. OK.

3. Now hypothesis AD re x-api-key: storage-level `sensitiveEventField` fragments: secret/token/credential/password/prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command. "x-api-key" not in ALLOWLIST anyway → dropped entirely. So no leak via generic payload. What about tool_arguments JSON? Keys inside the JSON string aren't checked for sensitivity at storage level! App-level redactObservableValue redacts sensitive keys inside arguments/result before JSON-encoding into tool_arguments/tool_result. Its key denylist: secret, token, password, authorization, cookie, api_key, apikey, credential, auth. Misses: "x-api-key" (hyphen!), "privateKey", "sessionKey", "apiKey" caught by apikey ✓ ("apikey" lower). "x-api-key": lower = "x-api-key"; contains "api_key"? No. "apikey"? No. "token"? No. "auth"? No. So a nested map {"headers": {"x-api-key": "sk-live-..."}} inside tool arguments → redactObservableValue recurses: map key "x-api-key" not matched → recurse value string "sk-live-..." contains "sk-" marker → wholly redacted. Phew — value-marker redaction saves sk- keys. But non-sk API keys (e.g., Anthropic keys start "sk-ant-", OpenAI "sk-", GitHub ghp_, google "AIza", AWS "AKIA") — "AKIA..." not matched by markers → persisted inside tool_arguments JSON. Hmm. That's a security finding candidate but weak-ish: attacker-controlled source? The provider events come from the runtime (agent), which echoes tool args. Tool args legitimately contain credentials sometimes (e.g., curl with Authorization header — "authorization" caught). "x-api-key" header name is common for Anthropic-style calls. The value would be persisted to run-control.db in plaintext. Consequence: secrets at rest in journal db readable by any local process/workspace reader (workspace-local trust domain says inherited posture...). The context pack §6 notes workspace-local trust domain as inherited posture. Given denylist intent clearly aims to prevent credential persistence, a miss like "x-api-key"/"private_key" is a genuine gap but requires the agent's tool arguments to contain such keys AND the storage sanitizer also missing them (storage sanitizer doesn't inspect inside JSON strings). Severity moderate, confidence medium. Let me keep it as a candidate and check tests (run_tool_observability_test) for what's pinned.

4. Now the big one — hypothesis S. Need Append behavior on cancelled ctx. Let me read sqlite.go Append and ProposeTerminal.

279: func (h *operationHub) finish(record *operationRecord, result app.OperationResult, runErr error) {
280: 	finished := h.now().UTC()
281: 	h.mu.Lock()
282: 	defer h.mu.Unlock()
283: 	if terminalOperationState(record.doc.State) {
284: 		return
285: 	}
286: 	state := "succeeded"
287: 	switch {
288: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled), result.State == app.OperationCancelled:
289: 		state = "cancelled"
290: 	case runErr != nil, result.State == app.OperationFailed:
291: 		state = "failed"
292: 	case result.State == app.OperationPartial:
293: 		state = "interrupted"
294: 	}
295: 	record.doc.State = state
296: 	record.doc.FinishedAt = &finished
297: 	record.doc.Result = projectOperationResult(result)
298: 	h.appendEventLocked(record, "terminal", map[string]any{"state": state, "reason": record.doc.Reason, "result": record.doc.Result})
299: 	h.active--
300: 	h.counters.active.Add(-1)
301: 	h.counters.terminal.Add(1)
302: 	close(record.done)
303: 	for id, subscriber := range record.subscribers {
304: 		close(subscriber.ch)
305: 		delete(record.subscribers, id)
306: 		h.streams--
307: 		h.counters.activeStreams.Add(-1)
308: 	}
309: }

324: 	defer h.mu.Unlock()

347: func (h *operationHub) cancelOperation(session, id, reason string) (operationDocument, bool, error) {
348: 	h.mu.Lock()
349: 	record := h.records[id]
350: 	if record == nil || (session != "" && record.session != session) {
351: 		h.mu.Unlock()
352: 		return operationDocument{}, false, errOperationNotFound
353: 	}
354: 	if terminalOperationState(record.doc.State) {
355: 		doc := cloneOperationDocument(record.doc)
356: 		h.mu.Unlock()
357: 		return doc, false, nil
358: 	}
359: 	requested := false
360: 	record.cancelOnce.Do(func() {
361: 		requested = true
362: 		record.doc.State = "cancelling"
363: 		record.doc.Reason = canonicalCancelReason(reason)
364: 		h.appendEventLocked(record, "cancel_requested", map[string]any{"reason": record.doc.Reason})
365: 	})
366: 	doc := cloneOperationDocument(record.doc)
367: 	cancel := record.cancel
368: 	h.mu.Unlock()
369: 	if requested {
370: 		h.counters.cancellations.Add(1)
371: 		cancel()
372: 	}
373: 	return doc, requested, nil
374: }

376: func (h *operationHub) subscribe(session, id string, lastID uint64) ([]operationEvent, <-chan operationEvent, func(), error) {
377: 	h.mu.Lock()
378: 	defer h.mu.Unlock()
379: 	h.reapLocked()
380: 	record := h.records[id]
381: 	if record == nil || record.session != session {
382: 		return nil, nil, nil, errOperationNotFound
383: 	}
384: 	if h.streams >= MaxConcurrentStreams || len(record.subscribers) >= MaxSubscribersPerOperation {
385: 		h.counters.capacityRejections.Add(1)
386: 		return nil, nil, nil, errSubscriberCapacity
387: 	}
388: 	if lastID > 0 && len(record.events) > 0 && lastID < record.events[0].ID-1 {
389: 		h.counters.replayGaps.Add(1)
390: 		h.appendEventLocked(record, "recovery_required", map[string]any{
391: 			"oldest_retained_id": strconv.FormatUint(record.events[0].ID, 10),
392: 			"newest_retained_id": strconv.FormatUint(record.nextEventID, 10),
393: 			"refresh_path":       record.doc.DurableStatus.RefreshPath,
394: 		})
395: 		h.appendEventLocked(record, "snapshot", map[string]any{"state": record.doc.State, "reason": record.doc.Reason})
396: 	}
397: 	replay := make([]operationEvent, 0, len(record.events))
398: 	for _, event := range record.events {
399: 		if event.ID > lastID {
400: 			replay = append(replay, event)
401: 		}
402: 	}
403: 	record.nextSubID++
404: 	sub := &operationSubscriber{id: record.nextSubID, ch: make(chan operationEvent, SubscriberQueueSize)}
405: 	if terminalOperationState(record.doc.State) {
406: 		close(sub.ch)
407: 	} else {
408: 		record.subscribers[sub.id] = sub
409: 		h.streams++
410: 		h.counters.activeStreams.Add(1)
411: 	}
412: 	var once sync.Once
413: 	unsubscribe := func() {
414: 		once.Do(func() {
415: 			h.mu.Lock()
416: 			defer h.mu.Unlock()
417: 			if current, ok := record.subscribers[sub.id]; ok {
418: 				delete(record.subscribers, sub.id)
419: 				h.streams--
420: 				h.counters.activeStreams.Add(-1)
421: 				close(current.ch)
422: 			}
423: 		})
424: 	}
425: 	return replay, sub.ch, unsubscribe, nil
426: }

428: func (h *operationHub) appendEventLocked(record *operationRecord, name string, payload any) {
429: 	name = stableOperationEventName(name)
430: 	record.nextEventID++
431: 	body := map[string]any{
432: 		"operation_id": record.doc.ID,
433: 		"time":         h.now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
434: 		"sequence":     record.nextEventID,
435: 		"payload":      payload,
436: 	}
437: 	data, err := json.Marshal(body)
438: 	if err != nil {
439: 		h.counters.projectionDrops.Add(1)
440: 		return
441: 	}
442: 	if len(data) > MaxEncodedEventBytes {
443: 		data, _ = json.Marshal(map[string]any{
444: 			"operation_id": record.doc.ID, "time": h.now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
445: 			"sequence": record.nextEventID, "payload": map[string]any{"message": "event projection exceeded the safe size limit"},
446: 		})
447: 		name = "warning"
448: 	}
449: 	event := operationEvent{ID: record.nextEventID, Name: name, Data: data}
450: 	record.events = append(record.events, event)
451: 	record.eventBytes += len(data)
452: 	for len(record.events) > MaxEventsPerOperation || record.eventBytes > MaxEventBytesPerOperation {
453: 		record.eventBytes -= len(record.events[0].Data)
454: 		record.events = record.events[1:]
455: 	}
456: 	record.doc.LastEventID = strconv.FormatUint(event.ID, 10)
457: 	for id, subscriber := range record.subscribers {
458: 		select {
459: 		case subscriber.ch <- event:
460: 		default:
461: 			close(subscriber.ch)
462: 			delete(record.subscribers, id)
463: 			h.streams--
464: 			h.counters.activeStreams.Add(-1)
465: 			h.counters.slowSubscribers.Add(1)
466: 		}
467: 	}
468: }

470: func stableOperationEventName(name string) string {
471: 	switch name {
472: 	case "snapshot", "progress", "warning", "finding", "artifact", "cancel_requested", "recovery_required", "terminal":
473: 		return name
474: 	default:
475: 		return "progress"
476: 	}
477: }

479: func (h *operationHub) drainAndWait(ctx context.Context) error {
480: 	h.mu.Lock()
481: 	h.draining = true
482: 	var records []*operationRecord
483: 	for _, record := range h.records {
484: 		if !terminalOperationState(record.doc.State) {
485: 			records = append(records, record)
486: 		}
487: 	}
488: 	h.mu.Unlock()
489: 	for _, record := range records {
490: 		_, _, _ = h.cancelOperation("", record.doc.ID, "server_shutdown")
491: 	}
492: 	h.counters.shutdownCleanups.Add(int64(len(records)))
493: 	for _, record := range records {
494: 		select {
495: 		case <-record.done:
496: 		case <-ctx.Done():
497: 			persistErr := h.persistCleanupUncertain(records)
498: 			h.markCleanupUncertain(records)
499: 			return errors.Join(ctx.Err(), persistErr)
500: 		}
501: 	}
502: 	return nil
503: }

505: func (h *operationHub) persistCleanupUncertain(records []*operationRecord) error {
506: 	recorder, ok := h.ops.(app.OperationCleanupRecorder)
507: 	if !ok {
508: 		return errors.New("operation capability cannot persist cleanup uncertainty")
509: 	}
510: 	var result error
511: 	for _, record := range records {
512: 		h.mu.Lock()
513: 		terminal := terminalOperationState(record.doc.State)
514: 		h.mu.Unlock()
515: 		if terminal {
516: 			continue
517: 		}
518: 		persistCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second)
519: 		err := recorder.RecordOperationCleanupUncertain(persistCtx, app.OperationCleanupUncertain{

reasoning_details.text:
Key confirmation: `canonicalOperationRequest` = JSON of the whole normalized OperationRequest (no nonce/timestamp). The TUI digest = sha256(canonical + "\0" + fingerprint). Fingerprint includes canonical + runtime identity + scope + hashes of governed input files.

So for the TUI: running the same operation (same request fields) twice with UNCHANGED governed inputs produces the SAME digest → second accept hits alias conflict → Existing → "matching durable operation already exists" card with lifecycle of the OLD run.

Is this intended dedup, or does it block legitimate re-runs? Consider the workflow: user runs "flow to plan" in TUI on sprint 35. Completes. Then edits... no wait — if any governed input changed, fingerprint changes → new digest → fresh run. But if NO governed file changed (e.g., a flow stage failed mid-run and user wants to retry immediately without touching inputs), the TUI refuses with "matching durable operation already exists" showing lifecycle "failed". Hmm — is that bad? Retry-after-failure is exactly when you'd want to re-run! The user's recovery path from the TUI is BLOCKED unless they modify workspace files or use CLI/web. Actually wait — can they re-run after fixing? If the failure was transient (network), retry blocked. This looks like a real operational defect IF aliases persist forever.

Counter-evidence to hunt:
1. Does retention/compaction delete operation_aliases rows? Check retention.go / Compact.
2. Does the TUI clear Confirmation between attempts such that digest differs? No—Confirmation regenerated each time from PrepareOperation; deterministic given unchanged inputs.
3. Maybe the TUI passes something per-attempt in req (e.g., Parallelism default set only for review)? normalizeOperationRequest might inject time-based fields? Check normalizeOperationRequest.
4. Is this behavior documented as intended ("dedup")? Sprint 35 requirements may say acceptance dedup prevents double-submit of SAME confirmation — i.e., protection against double-click, NOT permanent idempotency lock. A permanent lock on re-run would contradict "retry" semantics elsewhere (e.g., web allows re-run freely because token consumed once per preparation and each prepare→new token→new digest).

Note asymmetry: WEB re-running identical op works fine (new token each round trip). TUI blocks it. CLI blocks nothing. Three adapters, three behaviors — the TUI one arguably violates the product contract that a failed operation can be retried. Let me check retention.go for alias cleanup and check TRD/sprint docs for dedup semantics. Also verify normalizeOperationRequest doesn't add variance.

TRD L2079: TUI must expose "the same review/smoke scope, dry-run, confirmation, progress, cancellation, results, focused **reruns**, evidence links, and recovery behavior as the CLI." — FOCUSED RERUNS explicitly required in the TUI!

So the TUI digest regime (sha256(canonical+fingerprint), alias never expires) directly conflicts with:
1. TRD L396 "short-lived confirmation" — the dedup key lives 37 days (retention-bound), far beyond short-lived.
2. TRD L2079 "focused reruns ... same as the CLI" — CLI has no dedup (empty digest); TUI blocks re-runs of identical requests while governed inputs are unchanged.

Observable bad outcome: In the TUI, after a review completes (or fails transiently), pressing the same operation again returns "matching durable operation already exists" instead of executing — for up to 37 days. Retry of failed operations and re-review workflows are blocked from the TUI only. This is a concrete behavioral defect with contract backing.

Counter-evidence hunt:
1. Does anything vary between two PrepareOperation calls for the "same" request? canonicalOperationRequest marshals normalized req — deterministic. fingerprint includes canonical + runtime identity + scope + file hashes of governed inputs. Deterministic given unchanged inputs. So yes identical.
2. Maybe the TUI always passes a fresh Confirmation that differs because `req.Parallelism` gets defaulted differently? Only for review; deterministic anyway.

362: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
363: SELECT runs.run_id, attempts.attempt_id, attempts.owner_id, attempts.fencing_generation,
364:        attempts.host_digest, attempts.boot_id, attempts.pid, attempts.process_birth_token
365: FROM runs JOIN attempts ON attempts.attempt_id = runs.current_attempt_id
366: WHERE runs.terminal_outcome IS NULL AND `+predicate+`
367: ORDER BY attempts.lease_expires_at ASC, runs.run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, queryArgs...)
368: 	if err != nil {
369: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan expired run owners failed", err)
370: 	}
371: 	var candidates []reconciliationCandidate
372: 	for rows.Next() {
373: 		var candidate reconciliationCandidate
374: 		if err := rows.Scan(&candidate.runID, &candidate.attemptID, &candidate.ownerID, &candidate.generation,
375: 			&candidate.process.HostDigest, &candidate.process.BootID, &candidate.process.PID, &candidate.process.BirthToken); err != nil {

392: 				if errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) || errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {

413: 	}
